headline: Highest risk is medium: Copilot can write repo files while Great Expectations reads/writes validation artifacts, creating shared-workspace leakage and output-cascade risks; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot has no clipboard, MCP, or shell bridge, and Great Expectations has no documented inbound instruction channel. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff through shared repo files/open buffers, which is weaker than a direct parser hijack. Because both can touch files, uncertainty pushes this above none.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Great Expectations output into Copilot chat or files, prompt-injection risk becomes active.
IF both agents are pointed at the same editable repo files, file-based instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Keep Great Expectations outputs in a separate folder from Copilot-edited prompts.
Review any pasted validation text before sending it to Copilot.
Use read-only exports for Great Expectations results.
Disable automatic file ingestion into Copilot workflows where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while Great Expectations reads data sources and writes validation results. If the same workspace contains sensitive data, Copilot can transmit that context to a third party. Great Expectations is local-only, so the main leakage path is Copilot; the shared-file pathway makes this medium.
conditions: IF sensitive data is present in the shared repo or open buffers, Copilot may transmit it to its vendor API.
IF Great Expectations writes validation results into the same workspace, those results can be exposed to Copilot context.
mitigations: Remove secrets and PII from the shared workspace.
Use a separate repo or directory for validation artifacts.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive projects.
Redact data sources before running Great Expectations.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; Great Expectations can install packages and access files. In a shared repo, both can mutate overlapping artifacts, so conflicts are plausible even without shell access. The lack of explicit locking or coordination in either profile makes this a default-pathway risk rather than a rare edge case.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent edits can collide.
IF Great Expectations writes generated docs or tests into files Copilot is editing, overwrite risk increases.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches.
Serialize edits with a simple human review step.
Keep generated validation artifacts out of tracked source files.
Commit Copilot changes before running Great Expectations writes.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code or documentation that Great Expectations may consume as validation inputs or test artifacts. Great Expectations does not appear to critically verify upstream provenance by default, so a bad Copilot output can cascade into incorrect validation results or misleading docs. The pathway is inferred from their file-based interaction and is not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes files authored by Copilot without manual review, errors can propagate.
IF Copilot-generated tests or docs are treated as authoritative validation inputs, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of Copilot-generated files before validation.
Separate generated artifacts from source-of-truth data.
Add a checksum or review gate before Great Expectations runs.
Compare validation outputs against known-good baselines.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with repo-context access, while Great Expectations is local/open-source and touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. The pair can create compliance friction if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, but no specific residency or certification mismatch is documented here. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repo, Copilot vendor processing may conflict with policy.
IF validation results contain personal or regulated data, retention and logging rules must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review vendor and internal retention policies before use.
Use synthetic or masked datasets for validation.
Document which files may be sent to Copilot.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
